brief:
Gas shipments transiting the Strait of Hormuz reached their highest monthly volume since the start of the American-Israeli war on Iran, according to shipping analysis firms cited by Shehab Wire. September saw liquefied natural gas flows through the critical waterway surge to levels not recorded since the conflict began.

The flows continued despite regional tensions tied to the ongoing war, with trade moving steadily through one of the world's most strategically sensitive chokepoints.

title: Gas shipments through Hormuz hit war-high levels in September
